completion_data.completion_summary: The theorem library's tableau pipeline runs end to end at the user's ruled bound as one command. Six non-subsumed schemata are admitted as machine-generated registry entries that build sorry-free at [propext, Quot.sound], 2,981 certified refutations are written in the form theorem_library_countermodels will read without being admitted, and 2,895 non-admitted outcomes are registered as 48 aggregate conjecture cells. Non-redundancy over the generated entries is a build invariant.

sapience_notes.subject: Lean block comments nest, so one opening delimiter in generated text breaks the whole file
sapience_notes.value: A generated Lean doc comment that interpolates arbitrary text can be broken by a single opening block-comment delimiter, because Lean's block comments NEST: the inner comment it opens is closed by the doc comment's own closing delimiter, leaving the outer unterminated. The diagnostic is 'unterminated comment' reported at END OF FILE, which points nowhere near the cause. Found in BimodalLogic when a recorded reproduce-command carried a scratch path beginning with a slash and a hyphen. Any code generator must sanitize interpolated text, and the sanitizer's own docstring and tests must not spell the delimiters out either.

sapience_notes.subject: simpa can close a goal through Classical.choice where simp only cannot
sapience_notes.value: On Lean v4.33.0-rc1, closing a substitution-transfer goal with `simpa [f, g] using h` routed an arity-2 case through Classical.choice while the arity-0 and arity-1 cases stayed at [propext, Quot.sound] -- the nested ite chain of a two-variable substitution drags it in. Replacing it with `simp only [f, g, reduceIte] at h` then `exact h` gives [propext, Quot.sound] at every arity, because a closed simp lemma list cannot reach a classical lemma. Measured over ten generated registry entries in BimodalLogic. Where an axiom profile is a requirement, prefer simp only with an explicit list over simpa.

sapience_notes.subject: A self-subsumption filter implemented as an accumulating fold is order-dependent and misses real redundancies
sapience_notes.value: Filtering candidates by 'is this an instance of something already accepted?' in a single fold keeps both members of a pair when the LESS general candidate is seen first: the more general one that arrives later is not an instance of it. Measured in BimodalLogic's theorem-library pipeline, where 2 of 10 generated entries survived the fold and were then caught by the build-time invariant. The fix is a separate pass comparing every survivor against every other, with a STRICT test (A subsumes B iff B is an instance of A and not conversely), since mutual instances are renamings rather than redundancies.

sapience_notes.subject: A generated-entry admission rule must compare against the whole existing registry, not only against what the run has admitted
sapience_notes.value: BimodalLogic's theorem-library pipeline read 'unless it is a substitution instance of an entry already present' as 'already admitted by this run', and emitted 2 of 10 entries duplicating a hand-curated law. A compiled driver cannot walk the Lean environment, so the comparison set has to reach it as data: a probe exports each registry row's statement at the canonical schema variables via the existing tag-encoded formula codec, and the driver filters against it. The probe must import the hand-curated registration modules ONLY -- not the generated ones, or a run depends on its own previous output, and not the module where the invariant runs, or the probe is unbuildable exactly when it is needed.

sapience_notes.subject: A per-item timeout does not bound work that happens after the timed call
sapience_notes.value: In BimodalLogic's tableau pipeline, --timeout-ms bounded only the decision procedure; the tableau rebuilds that CERTIFY performs afterwards are pure, untimed computations, and the whole-run --deadline-s was checked only at the top of each loop iteration. One formula therefore held a 2,400-second budget indefinitely, reproducibly, at the same serial across three runs. Compounding it, records were written only after the loop, so killing the stalled run lost every record. Two lessons: a budget must cover every phase of per-item work, not just the one obviously expensive call; and a long run should flush its output incrementally so a kill is survivable.

sapience_notes.subject: ZTime gating in BimodalLogic is structurally unavailable, not merely rare
sapience_notes.value: The eight-gate route behind a theorem-backed refutation (not_valid_of_hasOpen_int) cannot fire at the ZTime frame class: regionLabel and temporalWitness evaluate false on every formula there, so BranchGates.gated is 0 of 11 while Base, Dense and RTime each gate 11 of 11. Confirmed at scale: a ruled-bound run produced 2,981 gated refutations, 0 of them at ZTime (Base 1,047, Dense 967, RTime 967). The witness-family certificate route through decidableCertifies is the only one at ZTime, and nothing in the tree derives such a certificate from a tableau branch -- they are supplied. A ZTime refutation count of zero is therefore the expected outcome and a finding about certificate availability, not a defect.

sapience_notes.subject: Fully explicit generated Lean source hits the 100-character and 1500-line limits immediately
sapience_notes.value: A derivation printed in fully explicit constructor form is hundreds of lines on its own: six admitted entries came to 2,053 lines in BimodalLogic, against a package-wide 1,500-line limit, and every formula argument passes 100 characters. Both limits are warnings, and CI building --wfail makes a warning a failure. A code generator for Lean therefore needs line wrapping from the outset (break on token boundaries, never inside a tactic block) and should pin a file-level long-file baseline to the file's ACTUAL length rather than a round ceiling, so later growth re-trips the linter instead of passing silently. Measuring the live tree for lines over the limit -- zero, everywhere -- was what revealed the limit was enforced before any code was written.

sapience_notes.subject: Json.mkObj renders alphabetically, so field order is a property of the source list only
sapience_notes.value: Lean's Lean.Json.mkObj stores fields in a search tree, so a rendered JSON object is in alphabetical key order and NOT in the order its toJson builds. Any schema claim of the form 'field order is <head keys> ++ <payload keys>' is therefore about the pre-render association list, and a test asserting key order has to read that list. In BimodalLogic's diagnostics records this forced each record type to expose toJsonFields and keys beside toJson; the golden strings are alphabetical for the same reason.
